# Tidepool
Tidepool is a self-hosted photo library for families. It runs on a Raspberry Pi or any
small server, deduplicates photos from everyone's phones, and recognizes faces locally
(nothing leaves your house). v1.0 ships next Tuesday after 18 months of nights and weekends.
Current users: ~400 people from the beta, mostly found via r/selfhosted.

segments.text: # Tidepool 1.0: your family's photos, in your house
segments.label: plain

segments.text: Somewhere in your family there's a photo of a birthday cake.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: Actually, there are probably eleven: one from each phone that was in the room, a couple more forwarded through the group chat, and one compressed screenshot of a screenshot.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: They're split across four cloud accounts, and nobody can find the good one.
segments.label: plain
plain

segments.text: Tidepool is my attempt to fix that without handing the whole family album to someone else's servers.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: Today, after 18 months of nights and weekends, it's 1.0.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: ## What Tidepool is
segments.label: plain

segments.text: Tidepool is a self-hosted photo library built for families.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: You run it on a Raspberry Pi or any small server you already have,
segments.label: supported

segments.text: point everyone's phones at it,
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README says it deduplicates photos from everyone's phones but never says phones are configured to sync/upload directly to Tidepool.

segments.text: and it becomes the one place your family's photos live.
segments.label: supported
plain

segments.text: It does three things well:
segments.label: plain
plain

segments.text: - **It runs on small hardware.**
segments.label: supported

segments.text: A Raspberry Pi is enough.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: You don't need a rack, a GPU,
segments.label: supported

segments.text: or a monthly bill.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README says nothing about cost or pricing; 'no monthly bill' is not stated.

segments.label: plain

segments.text: - **It deduplicates.**
segments.label: supported

segments.text: When five people photograph the same moment,
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README only says it deduplicates photos; detecting different shots of the same moment (near-duplicate grouping) is not stated.

segments.text: or the same picture comes in from three phones, Tidepool notices and keeps one library instead of five piles.
segments.label: supported
plain

segments.text: - **It recognizes faces locally.**
segments.label: supported

segments.text: Face recognition runs on your own machine.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: No photo, face, or embedding is sent anywhere.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: Nothing leaves your house.
segments.label: supported
plain

segments.text: That last point is the reason Tidepool exists.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README gives no motivation or origin story for why Tidepool was built.

segments.text: Family photos are some of the most personal data we have.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: Kids grow up in them.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: I wanted the convenience of "show me every photo of Grandma" without needing to trust a company's privacy policy to get it.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: Author's personal motivation and a search-by-person ('every photo of Grandma') feature are not in the README.

segments.text: ## Built with the beta crowd
segments.label: plain

segments.text: Tidepool spent its beta in the hands of about 400 people, most of whom found it through r/selfhosted.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: They ran it on hardware I'd never have tested,
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README says nothing about what hardware beta users ran.

segments.text: imported libraries far bigger than mine,
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README says nothing about beta users' library sizes or the author's own library.

segments.text: and filed the bug reports that turned a side project into something I'm comfortable calling 1.0.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README mentions no bug reports or beta feedback shaping the release.

segments.label: plain

segments.text: If you were one of them: thank you.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: This release is yours as much as mine.
segments.label: plain

segments.text:

## What 1.0 means
segments.label: plain

segments.text: 1.0 is a promise about stability, not a claim that it's finished.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: README makes no stability promise and says nothing about what 1.0 means.

segments.text: Concretely:
segments.label: plain

segments.text: <!-- TODO: confirm these match your actual commitments before publishing -->
segments.label: plain

segments.text: - Your library is safe to upgrade.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: Upgrade safety is not mentioned in the README.

segments.text: Future versions will migrate your data instead of asking you to re-import.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: Data-migration promise for future versions is not in the README.

segments.label: plain

segments.text: - The setup you do today is the setup you'll keep.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: Setup-stability promise is not in the README.

segments.label: plain

segments.text: - Breaking changes, if any, will be clearly documented ahead of time.
segments.label: invented
segments.note: Breaking-change documentation policy is not in the README.

segments.text: # Tidepool 1.0: your family's photos, at home
segments.label: plain

segments.text: Every phone in the house holds a different slice of the same family.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: The birthday is on one phone, the beach trip on another, and the good photo of Grandma is on whichever phone was closest at the time.
segments.label: plain
plain

segments.text: Tidepool is a self-hosted photo library for families.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: Your photos stay in your house.
segments.label: supported
plain

segments.text: After 18 months of nights and weekends, Tidepool v1.0 ships.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: ## What it does
segments.label: plain

segments.text: **It runs on small hardware.**
segments.label: supported

segments.text: A Raspberry Pi will do, or any small server.
segments.label: supported
plain

segments.text: **It deduplicates photos from everyone's phones.**
segments.label: supported
plain

segments.text: **It recognizes faces locally.**
segments.label: supported

segments.text: Nothing leaves your house.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: ## Why "nothing leaves your house" is the point
segments.label: plain

segments.text: A photo library that recognizes faces ends up knowing who everyone in your family is.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: We think that knowledge belongs at home.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: With Tidepool, the library is self-hosted and the face recognition is local, so it stays there.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: ## Thank you, beta testers
segments.label: plain

segments.text: About 400 people used Tidepool during the beta, most of whom found it through r/selfhosted.
segments.label: supported

segments.text: Thank you.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: This release is for you.
segments.label: plain

segments.text: ## Try it
segments.label: plain

segments.text: If you have a Raspberry Pi or a small server, and a family whose photos are spread across too many phones, Tidepool v1.0 is for you.
segments.label: supported
